q: Cathode rays are fast moving _____ emitted from the cathode of a discharge tube.
e: Cathode rays are composed of fast-moving electrons emitted from the cathode, as discovered in discharge tube experiments.

q: Cathode rays were discovered while studying the electric discharge through gases at _____.
e: The phenomenon was observed when studying electric discharge through gases at low pressure in a glass tube.

q: In a discharge tube, electric discharge first occurs at a pressure of about _____.
e: Electric discharge first occurs at about 20 mm Hg before the pressure is reduced further.

q: At very low pressure (~0.01 mm Hg), the glass behind the _____ is observed to glow.
e: At very low pressure, rays emitted from the cathode strike the glass behind the positive electrode (anode), causing it to glow.

q: Cathode rays were first observed in 1869 by _____.
e: Julius Plucker and Johann Hittorf first observed cathode rays in 1869.

q: The term 'cathode rays' was named in 1876 by _____.
e: Eugen Goldstein named them 'cathode rays' in 1876.

q: In 1897, British physicist _____ showed that cathode rays are composed of a previously unknown negatively charged particle.
e: J.J. Thomson demonstrated in 1897 that cathode rays consist of negatively charged particles, later named electrons.

q: J.J. Thomson measured the charge to mass ratio ($e/m$) of the electron to be _____.
e: Thomson found the charge to mass ratio of the electron to be $-1.759 \times 10^{11} \text{ C kg}^{-1}$.

q: The charge of the electron ($-1.602 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$) was measured by _____ in 1906.
e: Robert Andrews Millikan measured the charge of the electron in 1906.

q: The mass of the electron is approximately _____.
e: Combining Thomson's and Millikan's results, the mass of the electron is determined to be $9.107 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$.

q: Which of the following is NOT a property of cathode rays?
a: They cannot be deflected by electric and magnetic fields
e: Cathode rays can be deflected by both electric and magnetic fields because they are composed of charged particles.

q: Cathode rays can _____ the gases through which they pass.
e: One of the key properties of cathode rays is their ability to ionize gases.

q: The cathode ray tube (CRT) is a _____ tube that contains an electron gun, a deflection system, and a fluorescent screen.
e: A CRT is a vacuum tube designed to accelerate and deflect an electron beam onto a fluorescent screen.

q: Before late 2000 AD, CRTs were widely used in cathode ray oscilloscopes (CROs), television sets, and _____.
e: CRTs were the standard display technology for CROs, televisions, and computer monitors before being superseded.

q: CRTs have been largely superseded by newer flat-panel display technologies such as LCD, plasma display, and _____ displays.
e: Modern flat-panel technologies like LCD, plasma, and OLED have replaced CRTs due to lower power consumption and larger available sizes.
Cathode rays themselves are invisible; they only become visible when they strike a material and cause fluorescence.

q: When cathode rays strike the glass wall of a tube or a fluorescent screen, they can cause a glow called _____.
e: The glow produced when cathode rays hit a fluorescent screen or glass is known as fluorescence.

q: In a CRT, the electron beam is accelerated and focused onto the fluorescent screen to create _____.
e: The primary function of a CRT is to create images by focusing an accelerated electron beam onto a fluorescent screen.
